title: The peculiar chemistry of the inner ejecta of Eta Carina
question: What are the spatial distribution, kinematics and chemistry of molecular gas and continuum in the inner ejecta of eta Car, and how do they relate to the 19th-century eruptions?

what.value: Homunculus polar axis tilt of 49 deg used for inclination correction

evidence.quote: the polar axis of the Homunculus is tilted by 49$^\circ$

what.value: Average H2 column density of ~1e22 cm-2 through Homunculus walls

evidence.quote: provided an average H$_2$ column density through the walls of the Homunculus of around 10$^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$

recipe.method: Use QA2 cubes, convert to brightness temperature, make peak maps and 20 km/s velocity-binned HCO+ maps

recipe.goal: Measure continuum point source and extended component
recipe.method: Fit single 2D Gaussian to the point source and isolate the extended component

recipe.goal: Derive column densities and abundance ratios
recipe.method: LTE, optically thin emission with radiative excitation; temperature from dust equilibrium; for the absorbing bullet full radiative transfer with LTE
key_parameters: Non-detections: 3 sigma level as intensity upper limit
assumptions: Gas temperature equals dust temperature, T_dust = 13100 D^-1/2 K
Peanut distance approximated by projected distance, giving upper limit T ~500 K

recipe.method: Convert CO column to H2 with [CO]/[H2]=1e-4 for torus; express Peanut mass as function of HCO+ abundance

answer_key.quantity: HCO+ peak intensity of the Peanut
